claim: Without a prompt to use it, people rarely notice a stored analogue (about 30% vs 10% base), and a hint lifts success to about 75%. Noticing, not mapping, is the bottleneck.
agent_test: Run the same problem set with the analogue in context with and without a forced 'which earlier case fits?' step, at equal tokens.

claim: Retrieval of analogues depends on both surface and structural similarity, about equally and additively (69/38/33/13% pre-hint); after a hint only structure still matters.
agent_test: Vary source surface and causal match for the same target; measure unprompted retrieval by the agent.

claim: Unaided long-term retrieval favours look-alikes over true analogies (Karla: literal .56, surface .53, analogy .12, first-order .09) while people judge analogies as more sound.
agent_test: Plant a surface false friend and a deep analogue in memory; count which the agent retrieves and which it accepts after a structure check.

claim: Comparing two analogues and writing the shared schema raises transfer far above a single analogue (pre-hint 45% vs 21%; 47% vs 16%; total 80% vs 53%). Schema quality predicts transfer (correlational).
agent_test: Compare one-source mapping against two-source schema extraction at equal tokens.

claim: Stating the abstract principle alone, or one diagram alone, does not help one-analogue transfer; principle plus two cases, and diagrams after two cases, do help.
agent_test: Add a one-line rule vs a second worked case to the prompt; compare.

claim: Spontaneous transfer collapses after a context shift or delay with dissimilar analogues, but hints still work: memory holds, cueing fails. Rewording the target in schema vocabulary plus three analogues restored pre-hint transfer to 74% (confounded).
agent_test: Rephrase the target using the schema's vocabulary before retrieval; compare retrieval hit rate.

claim: Telling people to evaluate source stories, rather than summarise them, lowered later transfer (post-hint 22-28% vs 50-61%). Pre-hint solving was rare (1.3-8%).
agent_test: Ask the agent to summarise vs critique each retrieved analogue; compare mapping success.

claim: Case comparison beats other instruction in learning: d about 0.50 to 0.60 over 57 experiments, with similarities-only prompts and aligned features working best.
agent_test: Meta-analytic, from education; test comparison prompts on the agent.

claim: Structure-mapping is implemented as cheap broad filter then structural check (MAC/FAC); ARCS and ACME show a weighted sum of semantic, structural and goal cues predicts retrieval and mapping; a target constraint with no counterpart predicts failed transfer.
agent_test: Implement a two-stage O7 (embedding filter then relational check) and ablate the second stage.

claim: Systematic causal structure helps mapping when objects are cross-mapped, but only from about age 8; younger children gain nothing.
agent_test: Test cross-mapped analogues (same objects, different roles) with and without a causal-chain check.

claim: GPT-3 and later models can apply a supplied analogue (radiation, genie) and match students on letter strings, matrices and verbal analogies in default settings.
agent_test: Not needed; baseline.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: LLMs do not spontaneously retrieve the right analogue among distractors, but succeed after a hint: GPT-3 anecdote; GPT-4 0/15 correct source unhinted, recall 1.00 hinted with precision about .50.
schema_part: O7 (forced retrieval step) + code/verifier for false positives
agent_test: Replicate Puranam's matching task with a forced 'which case fits, and is it a true structural match?' step vs none.

claim: LLMs prefer surface-similar items over relationally similar ones in far analogies: ARN far analogy vs near distractor 29.1% for GPT-4 (human 96.0 mean); StoryAnalogy 37.1% vs humans 85.7%; AnaloBench accuracy falls from 89.1 to 60.7 as story length grows.
agent_test: Test the agent on ARN far-vs-near items with and without a relational-mapping step.

claim: Letter-string analogy results in LLMs do not survive counterfactual alphabets: humans 0.753 vs GPT-3 .488, GPT-3.5 .350, GPT-4 .452; GPT-3 below 10% on a shuffled alphabet; children and adults transfer to Greek/symbol alphabets, LLMs lose up to 0.50. With a code tool GPT-4 reaches human level on the shuffled alphabet (d04), so the cause is partly counting.
agent_test: Run counterfactual-alphabet variants on the scaffolded agent; check it stays flat.

claim: Dispute narrowed: Webb et al. reply that GPT-4 with code execution matches humans on the shuffled alphabet (P=0.496 vs humans), pointing to counting/indexing, not abstraction; Lewis and Mitchell, Hodel and West read the drop as weak abstraction. Task-demand effects are independently shown (Hu and Frank). Best LLMs match humans on re-representation (Musker 2025) but are order-sensitive.
agent_test: Run the shuffled alphabet with and without a code tool and with the rule stated in words; if only code closes the gap, it is indexing, not abstraction.

claim: GPT-4 story-analogy success is biased by answer order (0.89 first vs 0.61 second) and falls when the correct target is paraphrased (0.86 to 0.72, humans 0.78 to 0.70). The earlier claim of GPT-4 near-human story analogy is weakened. Order sensitivity also found in Musker 2025: Permuted Pairs coef -1.7 to -2.3, humans unaffected.
agent_test: Always randomise and swap answer order in any O7 evaluation.

claim: Self-generated analogues (recall relevant problems, then solve) help on GSM8K and MATH with strong models (text-davinci-003 50.3 to 61.0; GPT-3.5 75.8 to 77.8) but not with weak models; K=3 to 5 is best; failure is exemplars easier than the target.
agent_test: Test self-recall vs fixed few-shot vs retrieved at equal tokens on our model.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Gains from analogical prompting are small (about +1 to +4 points on strong models) compared with the retrieval-failure effect size in humans.
agent_test: Cost-benefit check: measure token cost of the O7 recall step against its accuracy gain.

claim: Analogical agent loops improve results: Thought Propagation (shortest path optimal 0.65 vs 0.33 IO, GPT-3.5), ExpeL (insights and retrieval each help, ALFWorld 40.3 to 54.4 retrieve-only), Buffer of Thoughts (Game of 24 82.4 vs 74.0).
agent_test: Each is author-reported with different baselines (three papers, but no cross-replication); reproduce one at equal tokens.

claim: Abstraction before solving (step-back) improves PaLM-2L: MMLU Physics +7, Chemistry +11, TimeQA +27, MuSiQue +7.
agent_test: Add a step-back principle step before mapping; ablate.

claim: Listing parts of the target before searching helps closed-set analogue retrieval but adds almost nothing for open-ended generation (Hit@1 24.5% vs 17.5%; open gains 0.4 to 1.6 points).
agent_test: Compare with and without sub-concept listing.

claim: A one-shot prompt showing the radiation analogy makes GPT-3 design analogies more useful (80% vs 40%) and less similar to the input; only the largest model writes human-level analogies (70.05% vs 66.67%).
agent_test: Small-sample, human-rated; check with a blind judge.

claim: LLMs stay far below humans on abstract rule transfer (ConceptARC: humans 91%, GPT-4 25-33%).
agent_test: Link to the ARC portfolio control.

claim: Inside Llama-3.1 the failure on abstract letter-string rules traces to missing stable concept vectors for abstract successor/predecessor (98% on known lists vs 62% abstract).
agent_test: Mechanistic; no scaffold test.

claim: Reasoning models (o3-mini, DeepSeek R1) collapse on analogical matrix rule induction under perceptual noise: 86.6% to 17.0% and 80.6% to 23.2% (chance 12.5%); 3.4x more reasoning tokens did not help, and high effort (2.7x) gave 0 gain on the hardest setting.
agent_test: Test frontier reasoning models on Puranam-style retrieval with and without a forced structure check, at equal tokens.

claim: Task demands, not only missing ability, depress LLM analogy scores: production vs forced-choice gap shrinks with model size (z=2.63, p=0.009); order permutation hurts LLMs but not humans.
agent_test: Always run each analogy test in two formats and two orders.

claim: Thought Propagation (analogous problems then refine) lifts optimal shortest-path rate: GPT-3.5 0.33 to 0.65, PaLM-2 0.14 to 0.36, GPT-4 0.78 to 0.88; one layer gives most of the gain. Synthetic graphs, author-reported, tokens not matched.
agent_test: Replicate at equal tokens on a real problem set.
